Decision `AP-DES-02`: whether to self-host Syne in the admin app (as the public site does) so display type matches the brand. Until decided, the existing fallback stays.

## 4. Layout and spacing

- 8px spacing grid; page gutter 16px mobile, 24px tablet, 36px desktop (matching `.ex-header`).
- Max content width 1200px; reading column 720px.
- Radius: 8px cards (admin `--radius-md`), 12px feature panels (as `.ex-research`), 999px chips.
- Elevation: borders before shadows; `--shadow-raised` only for overlays.
- Breakpoints: 640px, 960px, 1280px.

## 5. Components

| Component | Specification | Reuses |
|---|---|---|
| Portal shell | Existing header and tab navigation. Empower adds three entries: Academy, Resources, Knowledge | `ExpansionWorkspace` items |
| Search bar | Full width, 52px tall, silver 1px border, gold focus ring (3px, `rgba(209,178,102,.28)`), keyboard shortcut `/` | `.field-control` pattern |
| Course card | `--s2` surface, 2px gold-gradient top edge, overline (course number), title, one-line purpose, lesson count and reading time, progress ring (private), status chip | `.ex-panel` |

| Audience ribbon | Full-width strip above content: silver "Partner only: do not share" or gold-outlined "Client-facing: approved for sharing" | new |

| Knowledge result | Question (heading), client explanation (first), limitation, escalation, source, status chip | new |
| Copy control | Only on client-facing text; announces "Copied" via `aria-live` | new |
| Empty state | One sentence and a next action, as in the existing `Empty` component | `Empty` |
| Founder diff view | Side-by-side or inline diff between versions, additions in green, removals struck through, with labels | new |

## 6. Motion

Subtle and optional: 150 to 200ms fades for panels and chips, no parallax, no animated gradients. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (the admin already does for its workspace).

## 7. Accessibility requirements

- WCAG 2.2 AA as the target for these screens (an engineering target, not a public claim).
- Full keyboard operation, visible focus, logical heading order, skip link to search.
- Status conveyed by text and icon as well as colour.
- Lesson text resizable to 200% without horizontal scrolling at 320px width.
- Knowledge checks: answers announced via `aria-live`; no time limits.

[outside-nottingham] Yes. ScaleSmiths is based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire and works with businesses across the UK. Published work also includes CSDS, a computer repair firm in Pennsylvania. Projects outside the area, including work with businesses overseas, run remotely with a review cadence agreed in the scope. We do not claim overseas offices or regional expertise we cannot substantiate. Proposals are quoted in GBP.

[established-businesses] Yes, and that is where most of the client work sits. Confirm-A-Kill is an established Nottinghamshire pest-control business whose website and operating systems were rebuilt around search, conversion and day-to-day delivery. Established businesses usually have real evidence === rankings, enquiries, existing systems === and the work starts by protecting what already performs.

[hosting-provided] Yes. Published work runs on self-hosted Docker Compose and Nginx setups on a VPS as well as managed platforms such as Vercel, chosen around the workload and the support model rather than sold as an anonymous storage allowance. Hosting can be arranged as part of a build or as a managed service on its own.

[business-email] Yes. ScaleSmiths Managed Business Email starts at £15 per month for three custom-domain mailboxes with 5GB of storage each, and initial mailbox and DNS setup is included at no additional setup charge. It covers webmail, desktop and mobile client compatibility, aliases and forwarding, spam filtering, TLS-secured transport, and SPF, DKIM and DMARC configuration. It is available standalone, you do not need a ScaleSmiths website.

[deposit] Payment terms, including any staged or upfront payment, are set out in the proposal and signed order for each project rather than published as a blanket policy. Ownership of bespoke deliverables transfers once the applicable agreed fees are paid. Ask during discovery and you will have the terms in writing before anything is committed.

[ecommerce-builds] Yes. Pinkys Prints is a custom e-commerce platform with catalogue variants and a tailored product admin, migrated from Shopify. We recommend custom commerce only when the operational value justifies owning it; where an established platform already fits, configuring and integrating it is usually the better decision.

[integrations] Usually, yes. Published work includes a Salon Tracker booking integration and Google and Facebook review aggregation for Glow Tanning, and Stripe subscription billing with LiveKit video for The Business Circle. We check the existing system's API, data and ownership before committing to an approach, because not every tool exposes what an integration needs.

[crm] Yes, where an off-the-shelf CRM does not fit the workflow. Confirm-A-Kill runs on a private PostgreSQL-backed CRM covering enquiries, customers, properties, quotations, appointments, jobs, visits and commercial service records; CSDS has a quote management admin panel behind its website. If an existing CRM already does the job, connecting the website to it is often the better investment.

[stripe] Yes. The Business Circle runs Stripe subscription billing for tiered memberships, and Prymal uses Stripe for plans, team seats and execution credits. Card details stay with the payment provider === we do not create a reason to handle them directly === and order or subscription state relies on verified server-side provider events rather than a browser redirect alone.

[customer-portals] Yes. ScaleSmiths runs its own client portal for projects, invoices, documents, messages and requests, with tenant isolation enforced server-side. The Business Circle is a published membership platform with tiered access, and VeteranFinder includes member and admin applications. Permissions and tenant boundaries are enforced on the server rather than treated as interface options.

[internal-admin-systems] Yes. Admin surfaces are a recurring part of published work: quote management for CSDS, product and catalogue administration for Pinkys Prints, content administration for Glow Tanning, member management for The Business Circle, and a dedicated admin console for VeteranFinder. Roles, permissions and sensitive operations are enforced server-side.

[website-ownership] Ownership of the bespoke deliverable, along with content, accounts and any third-party services, is set out in the signed project documents, and transfer follows once the agreed fees are paid. ScaleSmiths keeps its own pre-existing tools, frameworks and know-how, and open-source components stay under their own licences. The client service terms state this in full.

[backups] Backups are part of a managed hosting or maintenance arrangement, and the order states which environments, data and retention are covered. We are deliberately plain about the limits: backups reduce risk but do not make loss impossible, they do not replace your own continuity responsibilities, and no restoration guarantee, recovery point or recovery time is created by our online terms. Ask, and the actual arrangement is written into the agreement.

[ssl] Yes. HTTPS is a build standard, not an upsell, and certificate provisioning and renewal are part of managed hosting and deployment. The specific arrangement depends on where the site runs: platform-managed certificates on a host such as Vercel, or certificates managed at the Nginx layer on a VPS deployment.

[dns] Yes, where you give us appropriate access. Managed Business Email onboarding includes configuring the required mail and authentication records, and website or hosting work includes the DNS changes a launch or migration needs. We use delegated or scoped access where it is supported, and we never ask for domain or registrar passwords through a public form.

[after-enquiry] The founders review what you send and reply with a sensible next step. That may be a few clarifying questions, a recommendation to start with the Business Growth Audit, or a proposal once the scope is understood. What can be committed to is the work itself: technical health, content that matches real search intent, credible proof, and measurement against a recorded baseline so progress is judged on evidence.

[wordpress] The websites and platforms in our published work are custom builds using technologies such as Next.js, React, Astro, Node.js and PostgreSQL rather than WordPress themes. If you already run WordPress, we look at what it is doing well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified.

[website-migration] Often, after a technical review of the current code, licence terms, data, deployment process and connected services. Pinkys Prints is a published example: a Shopify store rebuilt as a custom platform and moved from managed cloud services onto self-hosted infrastructure. We map existing URLs, metadata and internal links before a migration to reduce avoidable search disruption.

[hosting-included] Not automatically. Hosting can be part of a Growth Partnership or arranged as a managed hosting service on its own, and the order states which applications, environments, monitoring, maintenance and backups are covered. Managed Business Email is likewise separate unless a combined arrangement is written into the agreement.

## 1. Method and sources of authority

B0 still can't be merged properly, so I haven't started building B1. I did finish the full audit of all 27 B1 planning documents. [PR #155](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/155) is ready on the engineering side: still a draft, mergeable, at head `4e713e5`, with all 21 CI, Security and CodeQL checks passing. The problem is governance:

- I approved nothing, changed no settings and merged nothing. PR #156 stays based on the B0 branch, because retargeting it to `master` now would pull all of B0 into its diff.

## What the audit found

All 27 files were read in full and checked against the code and published sources. All 61 FAQ answers the docs cite exist, all 29 file paths exist, and every contrast ratio recalculates correctly. Fixed in this commit:
- **Lesson count:** there are 91 lessons in 38 modules, not 94 as the PR description said. There are no gaps or duplicates, and every lesson has text.
- **Commercial:**
  - Earlier six-month agreements (£4,100 minimum) were never mentioned. They're now described as historical terms that existing clients keep.
  - The "splitting payments can't change commission" claim now applies only to the current plans.
  - Refunds are described as recorded reversals, not automatic deductions.

The existing admin muted colour `#667085` fails on every background: it's used 68 times in 36 files plus 72 times as a class in 15 more. I recorded that for a separate, reviewed change rather than altering it globally.
- **Security:** blocking revoked or suspended partners is now specified, with tests to prove it. The existing partner check already does this.
- **Other:**
  - The objection playbook now gives each response's limits and the resource that backs it.

## Not done or not checked

- **Knowledge-check questions don't exist yet**, apart from one example question in course 1. The course outlines give only a question count, so there were no quiz answers to check. I've recorded this as deferred.
- I didn't fetch external sources such as the ICO guidance, or look at production settings.
- Accessibility was checked from the colour tokens only. There are no B1 screens to test yet.

The register is in [CONTENT-REVIEW-REGISTER.md](docs/expansion/empower/CONTENT-REVIEW-REGISTER.md) and the gate status in [B1-STATUS.md](docs/expansion/empower/B1-STATUS.md). The three uncommitted files in the main checkout were left untouched.

content.text:
Fine. To set that up I need the reviewer's **GitHub username**. Write access is the minimum level that lets their approval count; tell me if you want a different level. Giving me the username also counts as your go-ahead to send the invitation from your account.

The order matters, otherwise you'd lock yourself out:

1. **Invite the reviewer** with write access. They need write access for their code-owner approval to count, and they have to accept the invitation.
2. **Add them to CODEOWNERS on `master`**, next to `@TheFridey` on every line. This goes through a small pull request that they approve. GitHub reads CODEOWNERS from the target branch, so adding them only on the B0 branch wouldn't make them a code owner for PR #155. This has to land before protection is switched on. Otherwise that pull request would itself need a code-owner review, and you're the only code owner, so it would be stuck.
3. **Apply the protection policy to `master`** from `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json`. That means:
   - one approval, code-owner review, and approval after the last push;
   - all conversations resolved and the branch up to date;
   - 20 required checks;
   - no force-pushes or branch deletion;
   - the rules don't bind administrators.

   Then I confirm it matches the policy with no differences.
4. **Mark PR #155 ready and request their review**, with the reviewer checklist in `docs/expansion/intelligence/B0-MERGE-READINESS.md`. I merge only after they approve the final head and every check passes. CI, Security and CodeQL run on `master` after the merge; I found no workflow that deploys.

One thing to decide: because the rules don't bind administrators, your admin account could still bypass protection. Applying the policy as written leaves that bypass in place. Say if you'd rather have the rules apply to administrators too.

- **`AP-GOV-04`, approval rule:** a founder can't approve content they wrote while two founders are active. When only one founder is active, they can, but must record a reason.
- **`AP-GOV-06`, review cycle:** commercial content is re-reviewed every 3 months and service content every 6 months. Any item is re-reviewed straight away when its source changes.
- **`AP-ENG-01`, existing resources:** keep the current `expansion_resources` table as it is, add new content in new tables, and have a small adapter show the old resources alongside them.
- **`AP-ENG-02`, content formatting:** use a small, maintained Markdown library with raw HTML turned off. This is a new dependency, which I'll justify in the PR.

If you accept them, I'll write them into the approval register as your decisions, dated today. I'll then create `feature/operation-empower` from `master` and build B1.1, the founder content workflow. It covers versioned publishing, founder review and approval records, review dates and audience restrictions, with an audit trail and real PostgreSQL tests. The founder workspace sits behind a flag that is off by default. Nothing is published, deployed or made visible to partners.

- Tables `empower_content_items`, `empower_content_versions`, `empower_content_approvals`. Statuses add `changes_requested` (terminal for that version) to the model above; a rejected version is archived with the decision as its reason.

B1.1, the founder content workflow, is built and open as draft [PR #157](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/157). The founder Content studio sits behind `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED`, which is off by default. Nothing is served to partners, and no content item exists or is approved anywhere.

**What it does**
- **Database (migration 0091):** content items whose audience can never change.
  - Drafts can be edited; once a version is submitted it's permanent.
  - Approval records can only be added, never changed or removed.

  - Review dates are in UTC and must fall within 3 months for commercial content or 6 months for service content.
- **Service:**
  - A founder can't approve content they wrote while another founder is active. A sole founder can self-approve only with a recorded reason.
  - Required fields are checked for each content type, and every item must cite at least one source.
  - Links must be HTTPS and on an approved list.
  - Client-facing content that mentions things like commission is blocked unless a founder records a reason.
  - Withdrawing published content needs a reason, and every action writes an audit entry.
  - `servableContent` is the single rule later partner screens must use: published, within its review date, and matching the reader's audience.

content.text:
I've fixed a security gap in B1.1 that an automatic security review of the pushed commit flagged: one founder could rewrite another founder's draft and then approve it. The code only treated a version's creator as its author, so the editing founder didn't count as one. That defeated the rule that someone other than the author must approve.

The fix is pushed to [PR #157](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/157) as `e4dba3b`:
- **Server:** only a draft's author can save or submit it; anyone else gets a 403. Another founder can still archive an abandoned draft and start their own revision.
- **Database:** the approval check now counts both the creator and the submitter as authors. Someone writing directly to the database can't get around it by recording a different submitter.
- **Content studio:** non-authors no longer see the edit and submit forms; they get a short explanation instead.

I added tests for both paths. Locally, all 9 real-database tests pass on a fresh copy of the migration, and typecheck, lint and the migration checks pass. CI on the PR hasn't reported yet.

# Upgrade proof for migration 0091: master baseline (0090) with real history -> apply 0091 only -> compare.
# Temporarily hides 0091 from the journal/plan in the worktree (restored from git at the end; never committed).
set -uo pipefail
S="D:/Hermes/temp/claude/4ef63fda3fc46ec8/aebf5df5-fc53-46f8-adc5-609b4932802f/scratchpad"
B="/c/Program Files/PostgreSQL/18/bin"
W=/d/tmp/ss-empower-impl
PSQL() { "$B/psql.exe" -h 127.0.0.1 -p 55444 -U scalesmiths_ci "$@"; }
cd "$W"
"$B/pg_ctl.exe" -D "$S/pgdata" -o "-p 55444 -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1" -l "$S/pg.log" -w start >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
PSQL -d postgres -qc "drop database if exists ss_expansion_hardening_races" -c "drop database if exists ss_expansion_test" -c "create database ss_expansion_test"
H=127.0.0.1:55444/ss_expansion_test
export REDACTED MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL=REDACTED ADMIN_DATABASE_URL=REDACTED WEB_DATABASE_URL=REDACTED
# 1. Hide 0091 -> master baseline
node -e '
const fs=require("fs");
const j="admin/drizzle/meta/_journal.json";fs.writeFileSync(j,fs.readFileSync(j,"utf8").replace(/,\n\s*\{"idx":91[^\n]*\}/,""));
const p="scripts/shared-migration-plan.json";fs.writeFileSync(p,fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8").replace("\"through\": 91","\"through\": 90"));'
cd admin
node scripts/provision-postgres-roles.mjs --confirm-provision >/dev/null && node scripts/migrate-shared-test-database.mjs 2>&1 | tail -1 && node scripts/provision-postgres-roles.mjs --confirm-provision >/dev/null && node scripts/verify-postgres-privileges.mjs 2>&1 | head -1
echo "journal rows at baseline: $(PSQL -d ss_expansion_test -Atc "select count(*) from drizzle.__drizzle_migrations" 2>/dev/null || echo n/a)"
echo "empower tables at baseline: $(PSQL -d ss_expansion_test -Atc "select count(*) from pg_tables where tablename like 'empower_%'")"
# 2. Seed real history with the B0 concurrency suite (its guard needs this database name)
PSQL -d postgres -qc "alter database ss_expansion_test rename to ss_expansion_hardening_races"
R=127.0.0.1:55444/ss_expansion_hardening_races
NO_COLOR=1 EXPANSION_TEST_DATABASE_URL=REDACTED EXPANSION_WEB_TEST_DATABASE_URL=REDACTED \
  npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts test/integration/expansion-concurrency.integration.test.ts --pool=threads 2>&1 | grep -E "Tests +[0-9]|Test Files|×" | head -8
DIGEST="select string_agg(t||'='||n||':'||d, E'\n' order by t) from (select c.relname t, (xpath('/row/n/text()', query_to_xml(format('select count(*) n from %I',c.relname),false,true,'')))[1]::text n, (xpath('/row/d/text()', query_to_xml(format('select md5(coalesce(string_agg(x::text,%L order by x::text),%L)) d from %I x',',','',c.relname),false,true,'')))[1]::text d from pg_class c join pg_namespace s on s.oid=c.relnamespace where s.nspname='public' and c.relkind='r' and (c.relname like 'expansion_%' or c.relname in ('admin_users','clients','invoices','invoice_items','partner_applications'))) z"
PSQL -d ss_expansion_hardening_races -Atc "$DIGEST" > "$S/digest-before.txt"
echo "tables digested: $(wc -l < "$S/digest-before.txt")"; grep -E "^expansion_(opportunities|commission_ledger|payments)=" "$S/digest-before.txt" | cut -d: -f1
# 3. Restore 0091 and upgrade
PSQL -d postgres -qc "alter database ss_expansion_hardening_races rename to ss_expansion_test"
cd "$W" && git checkout -q -- admin/drizzle/meta/_journal.json scripts/shared-migration-plan.json && git status --short
cd admin && node scripts/migrate-shared-test-database.mjs 2>&1 | grep -E "Applying|applied|passed|Error" | head -5
node scripts/provision-postgres-roles.mjs --confirm-provision >/dev/null && node scripts/verify-postgres-privileges.mjs 2>&1 | head -1
PSQL -d ss_expansion_test -Atc "$DIGEST" > "$S/digest-after.txt"
if diff -q "$S/digest-before.txt" "$S/digest-after.txt" >/dev/null; then echo "DIGESTS IDENTICAL: all pre-existing tables unchanged by 0091"; else echo "DIGEST DIFFERENCES:"; diff "$S/digest-before.txt" "$S/digest-after.txt" | cut -c1-120; fi
echo "empower tables after: $(PSQL -d ss_expansion_test -Atc "select count(*) from pg_tables where tablename like 'empower_%'")"
# 4. Suites on the upgraded schema
NO_COLOR=1 EXPANSION_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$ADMIN_DATABASE_URL EXPANSION_WEB_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$WEB_DATABASE_URL npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts test/integration/empower-content.integration.test.ts --pool=threads 2>&1 | grep -E "Tests +[0-9]|×" | head -5
PSQL -d postgres -qc "alter database ss_expansion_test rename to ss_expansion_hardening_races"
NO_COLOR=1 EXPANSION_TEST_DATABASE_URL=REDACTED EXPANSION_WEB_TEST_DATABASE_URL=REDACTED \
  npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts test/integration/expansion-concurrency.integration.test.ts --pool=threads 2>&1 | grep -E "Tests +[0-9]|×" | head -8
PSQL -d postgres -qc "alter database ss_expansion_hardening_races rename to ss_expansion_test"
echo DONE

# Partner Academy knowledge checks (draft)

**Status: DRAFT. Not approved, not published.** Each question belongs to one lesson and is approved, published, superseded and withdrawn with that lesson's version. Every answer below is taken from the wording of the lesson it is attached to (see [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) and [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md)); a founder must confirm each one when approving the lesson. Knowledge checks are optional and voluntary, are never scored against a threshold, and never affect commission, allocation or standing.

Counts follow [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md): 65 questions across the 13 courses (5, 6, 6, 5, 5, 5, 4, 5, 4, 6, 5, 5, 4). The importer (`admin/scripts/import-empower-curriculum.mjs`) reads this file.

Format: `### <lesson> <question id> <single|multiple|true_false>`, then the prompt, then options (`- [x] id: text` marks a correct option) or `- answer: true|false`, then `> Explanation: …`.

## C01 Welcome to ScaleSmiths

### C01-L2 q1 single
Which of these is one of ScaleSmiths' published starting prices?
- [x] a: Website design and development from £2,000
- [ ] b: Growth Partnership from £250 per month
- [ ] c: Business Growth Audit at £595
- [ ] d: Custom platforms from £5,000
> Explanation: The four published starting points are website from £2,000, Growth Partnership from £350 per month, the Business Growth Audit at £395 and Managed Business Email from £15 per month. Custom platforms are scoped after discovery.

### C01-L2 q2 true_false
A custom platform can be priced against the website starting price.
- answer: false
> Explanation: Established-business transformation and custom platforms are never sold against a website starting price; they are scoped after discovery.

### C01-L4 q1 multiple
Which of these should an independent partner not do?
- [x] a: Issue quotes
- [x] b: Agree discounts
- [ ] c: Register prospects in the Partner Portal
- [x] d: Sign anything on ScaleSmiths' behalf
> Explanation: Partners introduce, qualify, register and support. ScaleSmiths scopes, prices, contracts and delivers, so quotes, discounts and signatures are never the partner's to give.

### C01-L5 q1 single
On the programme's availability labels, what does "Planned" mean?
- [x] a: Not built or not operational, with no date
- [ ] b: Live and available now
- [ ] c: Available once you finish a course
- [ ] d: Launching next month
> Explanation: Read the labels literally. Planned means not built or not operational, and no date is promised.

### C01-L7 q1 true_false
A meeting is booked as soon as you send a request in the portal.
- answer: false
> Explanation: ScaleSmiths confirms a time, proposes an alternative or asks for information. Nothing is booked until it is confirmed.

## C02 Professional Website Development

### C02-L1 q1 single
What defines exactly what a website project includes?
- [x] a: The written proposal
- [ ] b: The partner's meeting notes
- [ ] c: A standard package list
- [ ] d: The published starting price
> Explanation: A typical project covers messaging, structure, a responsive build, search foundations and an enquiry route, but the proposal is the list of what is included.

### C02-L2 q1 multiple
Which of these are separate from a website build unless the proposal includes them?
- [x] a: Hosting
- [x] b: Ongoing SEO
- [ ] c: A responsive build
- [x] d: Open-ended support
> Explanation: Hosting, ongoing SEO, content programmes, integrations and open-ended support are separate unless the proposal includes them. A responsive build is part of a website project.

### C02-L3 q1 single
A prospect keeps pushing for a price. What do you do?
- [ ] a: Give your own estimate so they are not disappointed
- [x] b: Give the published starting price with its boundary, and offer a proper quote or the Business Growth Audit
- [ ] c: Offer a discount to keep the conversation going
- [ ] d: Quote what a previous client paid
> Explanation: Never estimate a final price yourself. State "from £2,000", explain the starting-price boundary and offer a quote or the audit.

### C02-L4 q1 true_false
If a client asks, you should give them a likely timeline for their website.
- answer: false
> Explanation: Timing is confirmed after discovery because content readiness, integrations, review cycles and technical risk change the schedule. Do not give a timeline.

### C02-L5 q1 single
When does ownership of the bespoke deliverable transfer to the client?
- [ ] a: On launch day
- [x] b: As set out in the signed project documents, once the agreed fees are paid
- [ ] c: After twelve months
- [ ] d: It never transfers
> Explanation: Ownership follows the signed project documents and transfers once agreed fees are paid. Clients keep their own materials, trademarks and data.

### C02-L8 q1 single
A client wants online booking and customer accounts on their new site. What do you do?
- [ ] a: Tell them it is covered by the £2,000 starting price
- [x] b: Request technical scoping before saying anything about price
- [ ] c: Recommend a WordPress plugin
- [ ] d: Say it is included in every build
> Explanation: Booking workflows, customer portals, payments, integrations and anything with user accounts are not a standard website. Route them to technical scoping first.

## C03 SEO and Digital Growth

### C03-L4 q1 single
Can anyone guarantee first place on Google?
- [ ] a: Yes, with enough budget
- [x] b: No, because rankings depend on Google's systems, competitors and the searcher
- [ ] c: Yes, if the site is built by ScaleSmiths
- [ ] d: Only for local searches
> Explanation: No one can guarantee a position. ScaleSmiths commits to the work and to measuring progress against a recorded baseline.

### C03-L4 q2 true_false
Technical fixes can change indexation quickly, while content and authority work is measured over months.
- answer: true
> Explanation: That is the honest timescale: quick technical changes, slower gains from content and authority.

### C03-L5 q1 single
Is ongoing SEO included in every ScaleSmiths build?
- [x] a: No. Search foundations are part of every build; ongoing SEO is separate, as a project or through a Growth Partnership
- [ ] b: Yes, ongoing SEO is always included
- [ ] c: Only for sites over ten pages
- [ ] d: No SEO is included in a build
> Explanation: Foundations such as metadata, canonicals and structured data are built in. Content, authority and continued measurement are separate, scoped work.

### C03-L6 q1 true_false
ScaleSmiths will say when paid search is the more honest answer for a client.
- answer: true
> Explanation: Ads buy visibility immediately and stop with the budget; SEO compounds slowly. The right mix depends on urgency, margin and competition.

### C03-L7 q1 multiple
Which of these must you not say about AI search?
- [x] a: ScaleSmiths can get your business into ChatGPT
- [x] b: ScaleSmiths can guarantee your business is cited by AI tools
- [ ] c: Clear, well-structured answers help AI tools understand a business
- [x] d: ScaleSmiths controls what AI systems say about you
> Explanation: AI systems are run by third parties and change often. Nobody can guarantee inclusion or control what they say; well-structured, accurate content gives them good material to work from.

### C03-L8 q1 single
Where does diagnosing "we're not on Google" usually start?
- [x] a: Google Search Console
- [ ] b: Buying ads
- [ ] c: Rebuilding the site straight away
- [ ] d: Asking the client's competitors
> Explanation: Search Console usually separates the common causes (not indexed, not matching searches, competing above the site's authority) quickly, which is why the Business Growth Audit starts there.

## C04 Growth Partnerships

### C04-L2 q1 true_false
A Growth Partnership is an unlimited marketing package.
- answer: false
> Explanation: It is a scoped, ongoing partnership. It is not unlimited, not only maintenance and not a promise of results.

### C04-L3 q1 single
Until the founders decide how a minimum term is presented (AP-COM-03), what should you say about a Growth Partnership term?
- [x] a: Do not mention a term; the proposal sets the scope, price and terms
- [ ] b: It is always twelve months
- [ ] c: It is always six months
- [ ] d: There is never a minimum term
> Explanation: The twelve-month term is a proposed policy that is not approved. Until founders decide, do not mention a term.

### C04-L4 q1 single
In a Growth Partnership, what comes first?
- [x] a: Incidents affecting a live service
- [ ] b: Whatever request arrived most recently
- [ ] c: New design ideas
- [ ] d: The partner's priorities
> Explanation: Work follows an agreed roadmap and a prioritised backlog, not a first-come queue, and live-service incidents come first.

### C04-L5 q1 true_false
Hosting is always bundled into a Growth Partnership.
- answer: false
> Explanation: Hosting can be part of a Growth Partnership or a separate managed service. The order states what is covered.

### C04-L7 q1 single
A prospect wants ScaleSmiths to look after a site it did not build. What happens first?
- [x] a: A review of its code, hosting, access and update path
- [ ] b: ScaleSmiths takes it on immediately
- [ ] c: The site is always rebuilt
- [ ] d: The request is refused
> Explanation: ScaleSmiths can often manage a site it did not build, after a review. It will not take on an unknown system blind.

## C05 Website Migration

### C05-L3 q1 single
Can the search risk of a rebuild be removed completely?
- [ ] a: Yes, with redirects
- [x] b: No. It can be reduced, but nobody can honestly guarantee rankings
- [ ] c: Yes, if the domain stays the same
- [ ] d: Only for small sites
> Explanation: Any rebuild carries some search risk. Careful mapping and checking reduce it; nothing removes it.

### C05-L3 q2 multiple
Which of these reduce search risk in a migration?
- [x] a: Mapping old URLs to new ones with redirects
- [x] b: Carrying over content that performs
- [x] c: Preserving metadata and structured data
- [ ] d: Deleting old pages without redirects
> Explanation: URL mapping, keeping performing content, preserving metadata and checking indexing after launch all reduce risk. Removing pages without redirects increases it.

### C05-L4 q1 multiple
Which of these should you collect before a migration is scoped?
- [x] a: Who controls the domain and registrar
- [x] b: Search Console and analytics access, if any
- [ ] c: The client's registrar password
- [x] d: A list of integrations such as forms, booking and payments
> Explanation: Collect who controls what, access arrangements, integrations, licences and deadlines. Never ask for passwords.

### C05-L5 q1 true_false
A red flag such as a domain close to expiry is a reason to walk away from the opportunity.
- answer: false
> Explanation: None of the red flags is a reason to walk away, but every one is a reason to escalate early.

### C05-L6 q1 single
When does a migration go to ScaleSmiths for technical scoping?
- [x] a: Always, before any price or timeline is discussed
- [ ] b: Only if the client asks
- [ ] c: After you have agreed a price
- [ ] d: Only for e-commerce sites
> Explanation: Every migration goes to technical scoping first, with what you collected.

## C06 Bespoke Software and Automation

### C06-L1 q1 single
When is custom software usually justified?
- [x] a: When the workflow genuinely differentiates the business, existing tools cause real friction, or integration needs cannot be met by configuration
- [ ] b: Always: custom is better than buying a product
- [ ] c: Whenever the client has a spreadsheet
- [ ] d: Only for businesses with more than 100 staff
> Explanation: If a proven product already fits, buying and integrating it is usually better, and ScaleSmiths will say so.

### C06-L2 q1 true_false
You may quote outcome figures from published projects to make the case for custom software.
- answer: false
> Explanation: Describe what was built. Do not quote outcomes, figures or client opinions unless an approved resource contains them.

### C06-L3 q1 single
How should automation start?
- [x] a: With one bounded workflow whose owner, inputs, exceptions and outcome can be defined
- [ ] b: By automating everything at once
- [ ] c: By adding AI to every step
- [ ] d: By removing human review
> Explanation: Good automation removes repeated handling while keeping the decisions people still need to make; high-consequence steps keep a human review point.

### C06-L5 q1 true_false
ScaleSmiths sells "AI" as a feature in its own right.
- answer: false
> Explanation: Deterministic rules and integrations are often safer and cheaper. AI is used where interpretation is genuinely required, not as a selling point.

### C06-L6 q1 single
How is custom work priced?
- [x] a: Scoped after discovery, never against a website starting price
- [ ] b: From £2,000, like a website
- [ ] c: By the hour, quoted by the partner
- [ ] d: At a fixed published rate
> Explanation: Custom work is scoped after discovery with a defined first release.

## C07 Finding Prospects

### C07-L2 q1 true_false
Before passing on anyone's details, you should ask their permission.
- answer: true
> Explanation: Introduce people who would genuinely benefit, ask before passing on details, and be open that you are an independent partner of ScaleSmiths.

### C07-L3 q1 single
A prospect asks how long your lead protection lasts. What do you say?
- [x] a: Nothing specific: the lead protection term is not approved, so do not state one
- [ ] b: Six months
- [ ] c: Twelve months
- [ ] d: For as long as you want
> Explanation: The lead protection term, expiry and dispute process are an open founder decision (AP-COM-06).

### C07-L5 q1 single
Until ScaleSmiths approves a marketing process, what is the rule on unsolicited outreach?
- [x] a: Do not make unsolicited calls or send unsolicited marketing emails on ScaleSmiths' behalf
- [ ] b: Cold calls are fine if the business is listed online
- [ ] c: Marketing emails are fine if you include an unsubscribe link
- [ ] d: Anything is fine for business-to-business contacts
> Explanation: Direct marketing is regulated. Work through your own network and introductions until an approved process exists.

### C07-L6 q1 single
Someone asks not to be contacted again. What do you do?
- [x] a: Stop, record it in the portal and tell ScaleSmiths
- [ ] b: Try another channel later
- [ ] c: Ask why, and explain the benefits again
- [ ] d: Pass them to another partner
> Explanation: Never argue with an opt-out or try another channel.

## C08 Discovery Meetings

### C08-L1 q1 single
When preparing for a discovery meeting, what should you write down?
- [x] a: Questions, not conclusions
- [ ] b: A price estimate
- [ ] c: A proposed timeline
- [ ] d: The faults of their current supplier
> Explanation: Spend fifteen minutes on their site, search presence and reviews, and note questions rather than conclusions.

### C08-L4 q1 single
A prospect says "we're not sure what's wrong". What fits best?
- [x] a: The Business Growth Audit
- [ ] b: A full rebuild
- [ ] c: Managed Business Email
- [ ] d: Bespoke software discovery
> Explanation: When the need is unclear, the audit is the sensible first step.

### C08-L4 q2 single
A prospect says "our emails go to spam and we use a Gmail address". What fits best?
- [x] a: Managed Business Email
- [ ] b: A Growth Partnership
- [ ] c: Bespoke discovery
- [ ] d: A website rebuild
> Explanation: Deliverability and professional addresses are what Managed Business Email addresses.

### C08-L5 q1 multiple
Which of these should you not do in a discovery meeting?
- [x] a: Give a timeline
- [x] b: Mention your commission
- [ ] c: Mention a published starting price, with its boundary
- [x] d: Criticise their current supplier
> Explanation: No prices beyond the published starting prices, no timelines, no predictions, no commitments about what is included, no criticism of the current supplier and no mention of your commission.

### C08-L6 q1 true_false
You should write up notes the same day, keeping what the client told you separate from your own observations.
- answer: true
> Explanation: Use the questionnaire format: facts, your observations marked as yours, open questions and the agreed next step.

## C09 Presenting ScaleSmiths

### C09-L3 q1 single
How should you use ScaleSmiths' published work in a presentation?
- [x] a: Describe what was built, once founders approve partner use, and point people to the case studies on the website
- [ ] b: Quote the results the clients achieved
- [ ] c: Show screenshots of private systems
- [ ] d: Name clients you have heard about informally
> Explanation: Describe what was built as the FAQ library and case studies do. Partner use of each project needs founder approval (AP-PROOF-01).

### C09-L4 q1 multiple
Which of these must you not use as proof?
- [x] a: Testimonials or quotes not shown on the ScaleSmiths site
- [x] b: Outcome figures that are not in an approved resource
- [x] c: Claims like "we've helped hundreds of businesses"
- [ ] d: The published starting prices
> Explanation: Use approved, published material only. Published starting prices may be shared with their boundary.

### C09-L5 q1 single
What is the Business Growth Audit?
- [x] a: A one-time review and prioritised roadmap at £395; where the published terms apply, the full fee is credited against an eligible subsequent build
- [ ] b: A free trial of the Growth Partnership
- [ ] c: A monthly reporting service
- [ ] d: A guarantee of improved rankings
> Explanation: That is the published description of the audit.

### C09-L6 q1 true_false
Telling a prospect "this price ends Friday" is an acceptable way to encourage a decision.
- answer: false
> Explanation: Never use false urgency. "Would it help if I arranged a proper quote?" is enough, with an agreed follow-up date.

## C10 Objection Handling

### C10-L1 q1 single
What is the order of the objection-handling pattern?
- [x] a: Acknowledge, clarify, answer, confirm
- [ ] b: Answer, close, follow up
- [ ] c: Clarify, discount, confirm
- [ ] d: Acknowledge, argue, answer
> Explanation: Acknowledge without arguing, clarify with a question, answer with approved wording, then confirm and agree the next step.

### C10-L2 q1 true_false
Saying "that's a question for ScaleSmiths; I'll get you a proper answer" is a good outcome.
- answer: true
> Explanation: Stop when the objection needs ScaleSmiths: contract terms, technical risk, complaints or legal questions.

### C10-L3 q1 single
A prospect says "it's too expensive". What do you do?
- [ ] a: Offer a discount
- [x] b: Ask what they are comparing against, explain the starting-price boundary, phasing and the audit, and never offer a discount
- [ ] c: Agree to a payment plan
- [ ] d: End the conversation
> Explanation: Discount allowances are disabled and only founders could reserve one. Partners never discount.

### C10-L4 q1 single
A prospect already has an agency. What is the best approach?
- [x] a: Respect the relationship and offer the audit as an independent second opinion
- [ ] b: Point out their agency's mistakes
- [ ] c: Offer to undercut the agency's price
- [ ] d: Leave immediately
> Explanation: ScaleSmiths starts by reviewing what works, and the audit's findings are useful whoever implements them.

### C10-L6 q1 true_false
ScaleSmiths is opposed to WordPress, Wix and Shopify.
- answer: false
> Explanation: ScaleSmiths is not anti-platform. It reviews what the current platform does well, and configuring an established platform may be the better decision.

### C10-L8 q1 single
In the objection workspace, what may you copy and use with a client?
- [x] a: Only the client-facing line
- [ ] b: The partner guidance
- [ ] c: Everything in the entry
- [ ] d: Nothing at all
> Explanation: Read the partner guidance for yourself and use only the client-facing line with clients.

## C11 Commercial Policies

### C11-L3 q1 single
Under the proposed standard plan, which payments earn acquisition commission?
- [x] a: The build fee and the first Growth Partnership payment only
- [ ] b: Every monthly Growth Partnership payment
- [ ] c: Only the deposit
- [ ] d: The full twelve-month contract value
> Explanation: Proposed policy: 30% of eligible collected payments on the build and the first Growth Partnership payment. Later monthly payments earn no acquisition commission.

### C11-L4 q1 single
In the proposed standard example (a £2,000 build and the first £350 Growth Partnership payment), what is the total proposed commission?
- [ ] a: £600
- [x] b: £705
- [ ] c: £1,050
- [ ] d: £2,350
> Explanation: £600 on the build plus £105 on the first Growth Partnership payment. This is an illustration of proposed policy, not an earnings forecast.

For a Growth Partnership-only client, what is the proposed commission on the first £350 payment?
- [x] a: £105
- [ ] b: £350
- [ ] c: £35
- [ ] d: Nothing
> Explanation: 30% of the first £350 payment is £105 under the proposed programme.

### C11-L5 q1 true_false
The frequency and minimum amount for commission withdrawals have already been decided.
- answer: false
> Explanation: Withdrawal frequency, minimum, invoicing and partner VAT treatment are all open decisions.

### C11-L6 q1 multiple
Which of these may you do?
- [x] a: Share the published starting prices
- [x] b: Arrange a quote
- [ ] c: Agree a discount
- [ ] d: Describe your commission to the client
> Explanation: You may share published prices, explain the boundary and arrange a quote. You may not agree prices, discounts, schedules, timelines or terms, or describe your commission to a client.

## C12 Professional Conduct

### C12-L1 q1 true_false
As an independent partner you receive a salary or a guaranteed income.
- answer: false
> Explanation: The partnership is independent and commission-only: no salary, guaranteed income, compulsory hours or sales target. (Proposed policy, subject to solicitor review.)

How should you describe yourself to a prospect?
- [x] a: "I'm an independent partner of ScaleSmiths."
- [ ] b: "I work for ScaleSmiths."
- [ ] c: "I'm a director of ScaleSmiths."
- [ ] d: "I'm a ScaleSmiths employee."
> Explanation: Never imply employment, directorship, ownership or shareholding. The approved title is pending (AP-GOV-05).

Someone seems confused, distressed or not in a position to make a business decision. What do you do?
- [x] a: Stop and tell ScaleSmiths

- [ ] c: Ask a relative to decide for them
- [ ] d: Offer a discount to help them decide
> Explanation: Take extra care, stop, and tell ScaleSmiths.

Where should you keep information about a prospect?
- [x] a: In the Partner Portal, collecting only what is needed

- [ ] c: In a messaging app group
- [ ] d: On paper at home
> Explanation: Collect only what is needed and record it in the portal. Never ask for passwords.

### C12-L7 q1 single
You realise you told a client something wrong. What do you do?
- [x] a: Tell ScaleSmiths the same day through an escalation meeting request
- [ ] b: Wait to see whether the client notices

- [ ] d: Ask another partner what to do
> Explanation: Correcting a mistake early is always better than covering it.

For complex work you may suggest a rough price range to help the client plan.

- [ ] b: The partner
- [ ] c: Whoever is asked first

> Explanation: Brief ScaleSmiths beforehand, then let ScaleSmiths answer scope, technical and commercial questions in the meeting.

content.text:
Your usage limit was reached, so I stopped partway through B1.2. Everything done so far is committed and pushed to `feature/operation-empower` ([PR #157](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/157), head `62c106c`). Nothing is merged, deployed or published, and both feature switches still default to off.

**Done**
- **B1.1 re-checked:**
  - PR #157's CI was green on `e4dba3b`, with the content tests actually running under the restricted database roles; Web was still running when I looked. The new commits haven't been through CI.
  - **0091 upgrade check:** I migrated a database to `master` (0090), filled it with B0 history (89/89 concurrency tests), then applied 0091. All 58 existing tables came out unchanged, and the privilege checks pass. 0091 itself was not edited.
  - **Founder rules:** new tests show that faked authors or submitters are refused, and that another founder can't edit or submit your draft.
  - **One-founder case:** now tested on its own one-founder database: self-approval needs a recorded reason, and the two-founder rule returns as soon as a second founder is active. CI creates that database.
- **Migration 0092:**
  - Courses use the existing B1.1 versioning, and the database checks that a course only links real lessons.
  - Lesson completions and quiz attempts are private and can't be edited afterwards. The database refuses them unless the lesson and course are published, in date and linked.
  - Upgrading 0091 → 0092 left existing data unchanged.
- **Services:**
  - A course can't be submitted or published until every lesson in it is published.
  - Withdrawn or expired lessons show as "under review" with no content.
  - Quiz answers are never sent before an attempt and are graded on the server.
  - Marking a lesson complete twice records it once.
  - When a lesson is revised, earlier progress is kept but not counted as complete for the new version.
  - No commission code reads learning records.
  - 8 real-database tests pass, including a publish-versus-withdraw race.
- **Safe Markdown:** uses the `marked` parser (pinned 18.1.2) and renders straight to React elements. 30 hostile-input tests pass.
- **Screens:** the Content studio has a course editor and a quiz editor, so founders never edit JSON. Partners get an Academy dashboard, a searchable catalogue and a course viewer, linked from the partner sidebar, the onboarding toolkit and the meetings page.
- **Importer:** loads the 13 courses and 91 lessons, plus the 65 draft quiz questions I wrote, as drafts only. A second run changes nothing.

**Left to do**
- The committed browser suite. The disposable database is migrated and seeded, but the spec hasn't been written and no browser run has happened, for B1.1 or B1.2.
- Automated accessibility checks.
- Full regression: both production builds, the web suite and the full admin suite on the final code.
- An independent review of B1.2.
- Docs: `B1-2-ACADEMY-REPORT.md` plus updates to the architecture, status, security, acceptance and approval-register documents.
- Updating PR #157 and checking its CI.

Two known gaps: there's no partner "clear my progress" yet (waiting on decision `AP-PRIV-04`), and expiry can't be shown in the browser without superuser test setup.

input.old_string: ## 8. Open engineering decisions
input.new_string:
## 7b. As built in B1.2 (migration 0092): the Partner Academy

This replaces the separate `empower_courses` / `empower_modules` / `empower_lessons` tables proposed in section 3.2: the B1.1 model already versions, reviews and publishes structured content, so a course is simply a content item of kind `course`.

- **Course structure** lives in the course version's `fields`: `category`, `objectives[]`, optional `estimated_minutes`, and ordered `modules[]`, each with an ordered list of lesson item ids. It is edited freely while the course is a draft and is immutable from submission, like any version. `empower_course_structure_guard` refuses any structure that references a missing or non-lesson item, or repeats a lesson. Courses are partner-only (database check).
- **Publication integrity.** A course can be submitted, and published, only when every linked lesson has a published, in-date version; the lesson rows are share-locked while this is checked, so a concurrent withdrawal is serialised. Lessons are approved on their own, by a founder other than their author, so no one can slip an unreviewed lesson of their own into someone else's course. The course itself needs the same two-founder approval.
- **Serving (fail closed).** A partner sees a course only while its current version is published and in date and at least one of its lessons is too. A lesson whose current version is withdrawn or past its review date is listed as "Lesson under review" with no content. A course always shows each lesson's *current* published version, so a corrected lesson reaches partners without republishing the course.
- **Knowledge checks** are part of the lesson version (`fields.checks`: single, multiple or true/false, each with approved answer and explanation), so they are approved, superseded and withdrawn with the lesson. Partners receive questions without answers; grading happens on the server.
- **Learning records** (`empower_academy_completions`, `empower_academy_check_attempts`, `empower_academy_course_state`) are private to the partner, keyed by the server-derived partner id, and append-only except the "continue where you left off" pointer. The database accepts a completion or attempt only while `empower_academy_lesson_servable(course version, lesson version)` holds, and takes the timestamp from its own clock. A completion is unique per partner and lesson version, so repeated presses record one completion.
- **Progress semantics.** Current progress counts lessons whose *current* published version the partner has completed. When a lesson gets a new version, the earlier completion is kept and shown as "updated since you read it"; the new version is not claimed as complete. When a course is superseded, progress is recomputed against its current lessons; when a course or lesson is withdrawn or expires, it stops being offered and every historical record is kept. Progress is reproducible from these rows alone. Knowledge-check attempts are recorded (answer given and result) because the directive requires feedback history; this replaces the earlier "attempted only" proposal and needs `AP-PRIV-04` for retention.
- **Rendering.** `SafeMarkdown` maps `marked` tokens (pinned 18.1.2) directly to React elements: no HTML strings, raw HTML shown as text, images as alt text, links limited to HTTPS allow-listed hosts and Partner Portal paths.
- **Routes and switches.** `/partner/academy` and `/partner/academy/[course]` pages and `/api/partner/academy` behind `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED` (default off), independent of `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED`. The external-identity boundary in `rbac.ts` admits exactly these page paths for partners.
- **Importer.** `admin/scripts/import-empower-curriculum.mjs` loads the planning package (13 courses, 38 modules, 91 lessons, 65 draft questions from `KNOWLEDGE-CHECKS.md`) as drafts only.

# Operation Empower B1.2: Partner Academy report

Recorded 2026-11-20. Agent work and agent review only; no human review has taken place. "Implemented", "tested", "approved", "enabled", "published" and "production operational" are different states and are reported separately below.

## Baseline and delivery

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `feature/operation-empower` (draft [PR #157](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/157), base `master` `8950011`) |
| Baseline (B1.1) | `e4dba3b` |
| Migrations | `0092_empower_academy` (course kind, learning records, servability), `0093_empower_academy_partner_lessons` (review fix: partner-only lessons). 0091 untouched |
| New switch | `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED` (admin, default `false`), independent of `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED` |
| New dependencies | `marked` 18.1.2 (MIT, no dependencies; tokeniser only), dev `@axe-core/playwright` 4.14.0 |

## Status

| Capability | Implemented | Tested | Approved | Enabled | Published | Production operational |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1.1 governance (re-verified) | Yes | Yes (unit, PostgreSQL, browser) | Phase 1 decisions only | No | No | No |
| Course model, publication rules | Yes | Yes | No | No | No | No |
| Founder course and knowledge-check editing | Yes | Yes (browser) | No | No | No | No |
| Partner dashboard, catalogue, viewer | Yes | Yes (browser, axe, 5 widths) | No | No | No | No |
| Safe Markdown | Yes | Yes (adversarial unit, browser) | `AP-ENG-02` approved | n/a | n/a | No |
| Optional progress and knowledge checks | Yes | Yes | `AP-ACA-04`, `AP-PRIV-04` open | No | No | No |
| Curriculum importer (13 courses, 91 lessons, 65 checks) | Yes | Yes (parser, two imports, dry-run change) | `AP-ACA-02`, `AP-ACA-03` open | n/a | No | No |

No content item is approved and nothing is published in any real environment. The importer has run only against disposable local databases.

## B1.1 re-verification

- PR #157 CI on `e4dba3b`: 20 of 21 checks passed when inspected, with Web still running; the Empower suite ran (not skipped) in the restricted-role step.
- 0091 upgrade proof: `master` baseline at 0090, seeded with real B0 history by the concurrency suite (89/89), 0091 applied alone; all 58 pre-existing tables identical by row count and content digest; privileges verified; both suites green on the upgraded schema. 0091 → 0092 likewise left all 58 tables unchanged.
- Cross-founder tests: another founder cannot edit or submit a draft (403); the author cannot approve while another founder is active (403); a second founder approves; forged creator or submitter is refused by the database; approvals cannot be updated or deleted.
- Sole founder: a dedicated, freshly migrated `ss_empower_solo_test` database with exactly one active founder (the test refuses to run otherwise). Self-approval needs a recorded reason of at least 10 characters; the two-founder rule returns as soon as a second founder is active. CI creates and migrates this database.

## Academy design

See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) section 7b. In short: a course is a versioned B1.1 content item; its ordered modules and lesson references live in the version and are checked by the database; it can be published only when every linked lesson is an independently approved, published, in-date, partner-only lesson; partners always see each lesson's current published version; anything withdrawn or past its review date is "under review" with no content.

**Learning progress semantics.** A completion belongs to the exact lesson version read and is recorded once. Current progress counts lessons whose current version is completed. A revised lesson keeps the earlier completion ("updated since you read it") and is not claimed as complete. Superseded courses recompute against current lessons; withdrawn or expired courses disappear from the catalogue while every record is kept. Progress is reproducible from the stored rows. Nothing reads learning records except the Academy service (static test), so training cannot affect commission, achievements, referrals, allocation or withdrawals.

**Knowledge checks.** Single, multiple and true/false questions are stored in the lesson version and approved with it; a question cannot be submitted without an answer and an explanation. Partners receive questions without answers; the server grades, records the attempt privately, and returns feedback and the explanation. Retries are unlimited.

## Interfaces

- **Founder (Content studio, `/expansion` → Content):** create courses; edit title, Markdown description, category, objectives and learning time; add, rename, reorder and remove modules; add lessons from a list showing each lesson's status, reorder and remove them; build knowledge checks with a form; preview lessons and courses as partners will read them; submit, decide, publish, supersede, withdraw; version history and approval evidence per item; content-type filter.
- **Partner (`/partner/academy`):** welcome, continue learning, suggested starting points, catalogue with search and category filter, recently updated, completed courses, help and escalation; course viewer with module and lesson navigation, Markdown lessons, sources, optional knowledge check, optional mark-as-read, previous and next, escalation guidance. Linked from the partner sidebar, the onboarding toolkit's Academy item and meeting preparation, only when enabled. Resource Centre and Knowledge Base are labelled "coming later".

## Importer

`admin/scripts/import-empower-curriculum.mjs` with parser `admin/src/lib/empower-curriculum.ts`. Reads `CURRICULUM.md`, both lesson files and the new draft `KNOWLEDGE-CHECKS.md`; aborts on any missing or malformed source (unit-tested). Founder-authorised (active owner or administrator becomes the author of every draft), disposable databases only unless `--allow-database` names the target, idempotent (second run: 104 unchanged), version-aware (changed source with an open draft is reported, never overwritten), audited, drafts only. Every imported lesson and question passes submission validation, so a reviewing founder can submit it as is.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Admin unit suite (full) | see PR #157 update for the final run |
| Web unit suite (full) | 86 files, 468 tests passed (no web files changed) |
| Real PostgreSQL (local 18; CI 16) | Empower content 9, Academy 8 (incl. publication vs withdrawal race, duplicate completion race, client-facing lesson refusal), sole founder 2, B0 concurrency 89; privilege verification passes |
| Migration gates | history, order, consistency, checksums pass (0091–0093 registered) |
| Browser acceptance (`test/e2e/empower-academy.spec.ts`) | Passes on a production admin build and disposable database; screenshots in `evidence/b1-2/` at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 px |
| Accessibility | axe (WCAG 2.x A/AA and 2.2 AA tags) shows no serious or critical issue on the dashboard or lesson; contrast unit test for every Academy text and surface pair |
| Independent model review | No critical or high findings. Medium (lessons not restricted to partner-only) fixed by 0093 and service checks; low: date comparison fixed, stray empty file removed; feedback reveals the approved answer after any attempt (intended); importer `--allow-database` accepts any host (documented, drafts only) |

Browser journey steps, with how each was driven: founder login with MFA [UI]; studio [UI]; lesson draft with Markdown and a knowledge check [UI]; second founder sees no edit controls [UI] and is refused by the server [API]; author submits [UI]; author's self-approval refused [API]; second founder approves and publishes [UI]; second lesson [API set-up]; changes requested [UI]; course built from published lessons with reordering [UI]; course approved and published [UI]; partner opens the Academy from the workspace [UI]; search [UI]; Markdown rendered safely, script inert [UI]; knowledge check wrong then right [UI]; mark as read persisted after refresh [UI]; second partner sees none of it [UI, API]; partner refused founder API [API]; replacement lesson version reaches the partner with history kept [UI, SQL check]; withdrawal makes a lesson unavailable [UI]; review date passing hides the course and flags it in the studio [SQL fixture as the operator role, then UI]; revoked partner denied [SQL fixture, API].

Issues the browser found and fixed: the partner identity boundary blocked `/partner/academy` (now admits exactly the Academy pages, with RBAC tests); heading levels skipped from h2 to h4; links in text distinguished by colour only; the admin CSS reset removed lesson heading sizes and list markers.

## Known limitations

- No partner "clear my learning history" control yet (`AP-ACA-04`, `AP-PRIV-04`).
- No founder view of aggregate progress (`AP-GOV-03` undecided).
- Expiry in the browser needs an operator-role fixture, because no runtime role can backdate review dates.
- Lesson sources are shown as plain references, not links. Related resources wait for the Resource Centre (B1.3).
- Single-founder self-approval in the browser is not exercised (covered by the isolated database test).
- The "Continue learning" pointer is updated when a lesson is opened; there is no explicit "resume" button beyond the catalogue.

## Outstanding approvals before any real use

`AP-ACA-01` (switch on), `AP-ACA-02` (populate a real environment), `AP-ACA-03` (each question, with its lesson), `AP-ACA-04` and `AP-PRIV-04` (attempt history and retention), `AP-GOV-02`, `AP-GOV-03`, `AP-PRIV-01`, and approval of every lesson and course through the studio. B1.3 has not started.

## Summary

Operation Empower B1.1 (founder-controlled content governance) and B1.2 (the Partner Academy) on one branch. B1.1 adds versioned content with draft-only editing, append-only approval evidence, the two-founder rule, review dates, publication, supersession, withdrawal and audit. B1.2 adds Academy courses built on that model, a founder course and knowledge-check editor, the partner Academy (dashboard, catalogue, course viewer, safe Markdown, optional progress and knowledge checks), and an importer for the 91 planned lessons as drafts. Everything is behind switches that default off; nothing is approved, published or enabled. Full report: `docs/expansion/empower/B1-2-ACADEMY-REPORT.md`.

content.text:
B1.2, the Partner Academy, is finished and verified. It's on draft [PR #157](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/157) at `fe87fcf`, and all 21 CI checks pass. Both feature switches are still off, no content is approved or published, and nothing is merged or deployed.

**B1.1 checked again first**
- **0091 upgrade:** I upgraded a copy of `master` filled with real B0 history. All 58 existing tables were identical before and after, and 0092 also left them unchanged. 0091 itself was not edited.
- **Founder rules:** another founder can't edit or submit your draft, you can't approve your own content while another founder is active, and faked author or submitter records are refused by the database.
- **One-founder case:** tested on its own database containing a single founder. Self-approval needs a recorded reason, and the normal rule returns as soon as a second founder is active.

**What B1.2 adds**
- **Courses:** a course is a versioned content item, built in the database by migration 0092. It can only be published once every lesson in it has been approved by a second founder and published. Withdrawn or expired lessons show as "under review" with no content.
- **Founder tools:** a course editor (modules, ordering, lessons picked from a list) and a knowledge-check editor, so founders never edit JSON. There's also a preview of exactly what partners will see.
- **Partner Academy:** a dashboard with search and categories, a course viewer, safe Markdown, optional quizzes with feedback, and an optional "mark as read". Progress is private to each partner, and no commission or allocation code reads it.
- **Importer:** loads all 13 courses, 91 lessons and the 65 draft quiz questions I wrote, as drafts only. A second run changes nothing.

**Tests passed**
- **Admin:** 1,263 unit tests, plus typecheck, lint and production build.
- **Web:** 468 unit tests and the production build. No web files changed.
- **Database:** 19 new real-database tests, and the 89 B0 tests still pass.

**Browser run:** I added a committed browser journey that runs against the production build:
- **Coverage:** it drives every step through the real screens, except a few setup steps and server refusals that it checks over the API or with direct database fixtures, each labelled in the spec.
- **Accessibility:** the automated check finds no serious issues, and screenshots at five widths are in `docs/expansion/empower/evidence/b1-2/`.
- **Fixes it forced:**
  - Partners were blocked from `/partner/academy` entirely; they can now reach exactly the Academy pages.
  - Lesson headings skipped a level.
  - Links in text were distinguished by colour alone.
  - The app's style reset stripped lesson headings and bullet points.

**Independent review:** no critical or high issues. It found one medium issue: a client-facing lesson could end up in the partner-only Academy. Migration 0093 and service checks now block that.

**Not done or not verified**
- The browser journey runs locally only and isn't in CI.
- I tested locally on PostgreSQL 18; CI runs on 16.
- Partners can't yet clear their own history, and founders have no progress overview.
- These decisions are open and listed in the approval register: AP-ACA-01 to 04, AP-GOV-02 and 03, AP-PRIV-01 and 04.
- No human has reviewed PR #157.

input.new_string:
## 7c. As built in B1.3 (migration 0094): the Resource Centre

- **Resources** are B1.1 content items of kind `resource`, with `fields.summary`, `fields.category` (brochure, guide, checklist, template, reference) and optional `fields.related` (up to 10 lesson or resource item ids). Both audiences are served to partners; the audience ribbon says whether an item may be shared, and only client-facing items offer a copy control.
- **Search** (section 4, as designed, minus `pg_trgm` and zero-result logging): `empower_search_document(title, body, fields)` builds a weighted `tsvector` (A title, question and aliases; B body, summary and answers; C category and topic) from the immutable version, with a GIN expression index restricted to published rows. Queries use `websearch_to_tsquery('english', …)` after deterministic synonym expansion; ranking is `ts_rank_cd` plus a boost for an exact or contained title match, ties broken by slug. Filters (category, audience, published, in date) are in SQL. Query text is limited to 200 characters and passed as a bound parameter.
- **Synonyms** (`empower_search_synonyms`) are founder-managed in the studio; a synonym is switched off, never deleted or rewritten (database trigger), and every change is audited.
- **Legacy library (AP-ENG-01, freeze with read adapter):** published, partner-audience `expansion_resources` rows appear read-only, labelled "Earlier library", matched by plain substring when searching; client-audience legacy rows are never shown.
- **Downloads** return the approved version as `text/markdown` with its audience and approval details in a header, `nosniff`, no storage and no logging (`AP-PRIV-03`).
- **Related content:** a resource lists its related published resources and, when the Academy is on, related lessons with a link into the course that contains them; Academy lessons list the published resources that name them as related.
- **Routes and switch:** `/partner/resources`, `/partner/resources/[slug]`, `GET /api/partner/resources` behind `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED` (default off). The partner identity boundary admits exactly these page paths.
- **Importer:** the 13 resource drafts (`resources/R01`–`R13`) import as drafts with their stated audience; R13 is imported partner-only because the file mixes client templates with partner instructions.

- Read-only for partners (`GET` only); behind `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED` and `partnerGuard`. Only published, in-date resources are returned; withdrawal takes effect on the next request.

content.text:
B1.3, the Resource Centre, is finished and verified. It's on draft [PR #157](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/157) at `64d86b1`, and all 21 CI checks pass. Its switch, `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED`, defaults to off, and no resource is approved or published.

**What it adds**
- **Search:** migration 0094 adds PostgreSQL full-text search over published resources only. Results are ranked and filtered in the database, and the same query always returns the same order.
- **Synonyms:** founders manage them in the studio. For example, a search for "ssl" also finds "https certificate". A synonym is switched off rather than edited or deleted, and every change is logged.
- **Partner Resource Centre (`/partner/resources`):**
  - search with category and audience filters, and a label on each resource saying whether it may be shared;
  - a "Copy for a client" button, only on client-facing resources;
  - a download of the approved text with its approval details;
  - links between related lessons and resources, in both directions;
  - the old B0 resource library, shown read-only and labelled.
- **Founder tools:** a picker for related lessons and resources, and a synonyms panel.
- **Importer:** all 13 resource drafts load as drafts with the audience stated in each file. A re-run reports all 117 curriculum and resource items unchanged.

**Tests passed**
- **Admin:** typecheck and lint clean; full suite 1,269 tests (4 skipped, as before).
- **Database:** 7 new Resource Centre tests, and the earlier Empower suites still pass.
- **Browser:** the B1.1/B1.2 journey and a new Resource Centre journey both pass on a production build. The automated accessibility check found no serious issues, and nothing overflows at any of the five screen widths. Screenshots are in `docs/expansion/empower/evidence/b1-3/`.

**Problems caught and fixed**
- R08's audience reads "Partner only, with client-facing lines marked", and the importer was classing it as client-facing. A test caught it before anything was imported.
- The independent review found no critical or high issues. I fixed what it raised: two stray empty files, a stricter slug check, older duplicate versions in the old library, and synonym text that could alter the search query.
- CI's Web job failed its performance-budget check once. No web files changed, and it passed on a single rerun, so I treated it as timing variation on the CI machine.

**Open decisions and gaps**
- R13 is imported as partner-only, because the file mixes client templates with partner instructions; whether to keep it that way is decision AP-RES-03.
- Search doesn't log zero-result queries, and its speed target hasn't been load-tested.
- Before switching the Resource Centre on, AP-RES-01 to 03 and AP-PUB-02 need your decision, and each resource needs approval in the studio.
- No one has reviewed PR #157 yet.

## 7d. As built in B1.4 (no migration): the Knowledge Base

- **Entries** are B1.1 content items of kind `knowledge` with the section 3.3 fields (question, answer, client explanation, limitation, escalation rule, condition and meeting route, aliases, topic). A knowledge version cannot be submitted without them.
- **Search** reuses `empower_search_document` and the synonyms from B1.3. An exact match on the question or any alias (case-insensitive, trailing punctuation ignored) adds a fixed boost so it always ranks first; then `ts_rank_cd`; ties by slug. Topic filtering is in SQL against the approved topic list.
- **Partner view** (`/partner/knowledge`, switch `PARTNER_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ENABLED`, default off): search-first with the input focused and `/` to refocus; topic chips; the top result expanded; the client explanation first with a copy control only for client-facing entries; the precise answer, limitation, escalation rule and sources; related published resources.
- **Escalation** uses the existing B0 meeting request (`request_meeting` on `/api/partner`), pre-filled with the entry's route and reference. The server derives the partner from the session; nothing is booked until a founder confirms. A search with no approved answer offers the same request instead of a guess.
- **Importer:** the 32 planned entries import as drafts. Client explanations that point at the objection playbook or the pricing reference resolve to that approved wording; an entry naming more than one escalation route is refused; entries with no client-safe explanation are partner-only.

# Operation Empower B1.4: Knowledge Base report

Recorded 2026-11-20. Agent work only; no human review. "Implemented", "tested", "approved", "enabled" and "published" are reported separately.

## Scope delivered

| Capability | Implemented | Tested | Approved | Enabled | Published |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Approved knowledge entries (governed content, required fields) | Yes (B1.1 model) | Unit, PostgreSQL, browser | No | No | No |
| Deterministic search with exact alias or question match first, synonyms, topic filter | Yes | PostgreSQL, browser | n/a | No | n/a |
| Partner Knowledge Base page (search-first, client line and copy, limitation, escalation, sources, related resources) | Yes | Browser, axe, 5 widths | No | No | No |
| "Request help" through the existing meeting request; no-answer state | Yes | Browser and SQL check | n/a | No | n/a |
| 32 planned entries imported as drafts | Yes | Parser, imports | `AP-KB-02` and each entry open | n/a | No |

No migration: B1.4 reuses the B1.1 content model and the B1.3 search document and synonyms. New switch `PARTNER_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ENABLED` (default `false`). The partner identity boundary now also admits exactly `/partner/knowledge`.

## A correction to the planning package

The package summary and the content review register said 33 knowledge entries. `KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md` contains 32, and the per-topic counts in the register also total 32. The register is corrected, and the importer now requires exactly 32.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Admin lint, full unit suite | Clean; 167 files, 1,271 passed, 4 skipped (pre-existing) before the review fixes; parser suite 11 passed after them |
| Empower PostgreSQL suites (content, Academy, Resource Centre, Knowledge Base) | 28 passed as the restricted admin role |
| Knowledge Base integration (4) | Switch and identity refusals; alias and question matches rank first and repeat identically; full entry shape; partner-only entry without a client line; topic allow-list; drafts and withdrawn entries excluded; related published resources |
| Parser | All 32 entries parse, resolve their client explanations (objection lines, pricing boundary, "as answer") and pass submission, including the client-facing audience check, with no override |
| Browser (production build, disposable database) | All three journeys pass: B1.1/B1.2, B1.3 and the new B1.4. Founder drafts an entry with an alias [UI]; second founder approves and publishes [UI]; partner opens the Knowledge Base from the workspace with the search box focused [UI], searches the way a client asked and gets the entry first with its client line and copy control [UI]; requests help [UI] and a normal meeting request exists, not confirmed [SQL check]; an unanswered question offers help [UI]; withdrawal removes the entry [UI]. axe clean of serious issues; no overflow at 320 to 1440 px; screenshots in `evidence/b1-4/` |
| Independent model review | No critical or high findings. Fixed: an entry naming two escalation routes is now refused instead of silently keeping the first (KB-SEC-01 reworded, `AP-KB-02`); entries with no client explanation are partner-only whatever their topic; a stray empty file removed. Accepted: exact matching ignores only trailing punctuation |

## Limitations

- Exact alias matching normalises case and trailing punctuation, not inner spacing.
- Searches are not logged, so founders cannot yet see unanswered questions (`AP-PRIV-02`).
- The objection-handling workspace (B1.5) is not built; the objection playbook is available as resource R08.

## Outstanding approvals

`AP-KB-01` (switch on), `AP-KB-02` (KB-SEC-01 wording), `AP-PRIV-01` and `AP-PRIV-02`, and approval of each entry through the studio.

- **Search:** partners at `/partner/knowledge` type the question the way a client asked it. An exact match on the question or one of its aliases always comes first. It uses the B1.3 search and synonyms, so no migration was needed.

The cause was a flaw in the tests, not the product: each test builds a search word from a random ID with the digits removed, and this run's ID was all digits, so the word came out empty. I fixed it in both database suites and the browser spec, and pushed the fix as `b215546`. The next run passed in full.

- The objection-handling workspace (B1.5) hasn't been started.
